summary: The change sends Google sign-in cancellations and failures back to the desktop loopback callback, and it moves desktop sign-in out of the auth queue. It also blocks connection retries while sign-in is required and replaces the connection dialog with an accessible react-aria modal. It is not ready to merge. The coverage gate fails with 21 uncovered lines. A retry guard also leaves the "authentication" state with no automatic way out, so a tab whose credentials became valid elsewhere no longer recovers on focus or reconnect.

findings.body: The new `this.state.status === "authentication"` guards in `retry` (line 110) and `reportActivity` (line 444) leave the authentication state with no automatic way out. The `online`, `focus`, `visibilitychange` and worker-`running` events all go through these two paths, so after `failed()` publishes "authentication" the service never calls `connect()` again unless the user clicks Sign in. Before this change, a focus or visibility event re-ran `connect()`. That recovered a tab whose credentials became valid somewhere else, for example a second browser tab that signed in again, where WebHost.signIn redirects the whole page, or a stale UNAUTHORIZED in local development. Now the only way out in the web app is a full-page Google redirect, which discards in-memory UI state that a focus event used to keep. The goal seems to be keeping the dialog from flickering while sign-in is in progress. Limit the guard to that case: skip retries only while a sign-in is running (for example a `signingIn` flag that the dialog sets or `resumeAfterSignIn` clears). Or keep focus and online retries in the authentication state but have `connect()` leave the published status alone until it succeeds. Add a test showing that a tab in the authentication state reconnects on focus once `getConnection` returns a valid connection again.

testRequests.rationale: These lines are reported as uncovered. The e2e test runs some of them (concurrent signIn, final token write, error and empty-code callbacks), but the coverage collected from the esbuild bundle inside Electron main is mapped only in part. Add a reliable temp Vitest test for ControlPlaneAuth with `electron` mocked (safeStorage, openExternalUrl), or fix the bundle's source-map coverage collection. The test must assert these behaviors: a second signIn() call while one is pending returns the same promise and opens only one URL; getWorkspaceConnection() with no token returns AuthenticationRequiredError and stays responsive during a pending sign-in; an `error=access_denied` callback resolves to DesktopSignInCancelledError and other errors resolve to ControlPlaneAuthError; a wrong state, path or method, or a missing or empty code, gets 400 and leaves the promise pending; a successful exchange writes the token through the queue and getSession() then returns the session.

The coverage report lists this line as uncovered. Find out which branch it maps to; it may be the fall-through where callback or state is missing, or the case where only one of the two is present. Cover it with a request that asserts the response: for example `callback` without `state` should fall through to the 200 plain-text page and must not redirect.

F1 needs a regression test: in the authentication state, a focus or online event either reconnects once the host returns a valid connection, or is deliberately skipped only while a sign-in is in progress.
